entries.condition: Glass not resolvable at this distance; scored from code.
entries.evidence: Cabin glass is a few pixels; no sorting artefacts resolvable.
entries.defect: src/plane/model.ts:59-73: the glass is one DoubleSide MeshPhysicalMaterial mesh with depthWrite=false, opacity driven by an ad-hoc (1-NdotV)^3 alpha ramp (0.22 -> 0.85) instead of a reflectance Fresnel, so panes darken/turn opaque at grazing angles rather than becoming mirror-like; overlapping panes inside a single mesh are composited in triangle order (mis-sorting), the loft faces are flat-shaded so the ramp is faceted, and the PMREM environment is a sky-only dome (no sun disc), so there is no sun highlight in the glass.
entries.fix: Keep alpha constant (~0.15) and let specular Fresnel (specularIntensity/ior, clearcoat) carry the view dependence; render inner and outer glass as two FrontSide meshes with renderOrder outer>inner; smooth the glass normals (computeVertexNormals on the indexed loft before splitGlass); add the sun disc/skyRadiance to the envScene so reflections carry a highlight.

entries.condition: Downtown skyline upper-left, suburbs across the mainland and on Isla Garza.
entries.evidence: Skyline tallest-tower displacement 0.028 (score 8); towers are clean boxes with procedural facades; mainland suburb houses are 1-3 px specks that alias into a uniform stipple - the per-pixel roof branch flip verified in the cloudy close-up randomises each roof pixel and feeds that stipple (not individually resolvable here).
entries.defect: src/world/facade.ts: window/tile patterns are step() functions of world position with only a fwidth-based 'lod' blend applied to colour; the emissive term (lines 118/129/143/157/180) is not attenuated by lod, and MSAA does not filter shader aliasing, so sub-pixel windows and 0.35 m tile rows alias into speckle at distance. src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding.
entries.fix: Multiply emis by (1.0 - lod) and blend to the average lit fraction, pre-filter the patterns analytically (box-filtered step) or bake facades to a mip-mapped atlas; add TAA or increase MSAA for thin geometry. Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback.

entries.evidence: Trees are dark low-poly puffs; probe: vegetation = 4,898,856 triangles of 7,005,278.

entries.condition: Cumulus band across the top of the frame.

entries.condition: renderer.info counters and 8-frame synchronous profile vs a 60 FPS desktop budget (<=400 calls, <=1.5 M tris). Frames come from headless Chrome on SwiftShader (software rasterizer), so absolute frame times (3-5 s per 1080p frame) are not representative of a desktop GPU; relative cost, counters and spread are evaluated instead.
entries.evidence: renderer.info: 1283 draw calls (3.2x the 400-call budget), 7.01 M triangles (4.7x the 1.5 M budget), 631 geometries, 41 textures, 40 programs, JS heap 119 MB; bench profile of 8 synchronous frames: avg 4495 ms, min 4341, max 4786 (spread 9.9% of avg). Probe (toggling scene groups on the same build, 960x540, counters are resolution independent): shadow pass = 515 calls / 3.90 M tris; vegetation = 252 calls / 4.90 M tris (70% of all triangles); city = 280 calls / 0.51 M; props = 77 calls / 0.76 M; traffic = 240 calls / 0.19 M; aircraft = 338 calls for only 22 k tris; camera pointed at the zenith still draws 840 calls / 6.96 M tris (frustum culling is effectively off). console.txt is 0 bytes for all 13 views (no shader-compile, texture, WebGL or deprecation messages during capture) and the probe pages logged nothing either.
entries.defect: Every view is 2.7-3.8x over the draw-call budget and 2.4-5.9x over the triangle budget: (a) frustum culling is defeated - src/world/vegetation.ts:328 and src/world/city.ts:170 store a WORLD-space sphere in geometry.boundingSphere, which InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere() then transforms by every instance matrix (centre x scale ~10, radius km) so no tile is ever culled, while props.ts:69/75, traffic.ts:306 (all cars), game.ts:175 (lamps), bridges.ts:217-232, roads.ts:210 set frustumCulled=false; (b) the 3-cascade CSM re-draws every caster up to 3 more times (shadow pass = 30-57% of triangles); (c) icosahedron-puff canopies make vegetation 43-72% of all triangles; (d) the aircraft is ~85 separate meshes (232-444 draw calls for ~22 k triangles). Frame-time spread in this view is 9.9% of the mean (no streaming stutter observed). Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
entries.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).

entries.evidence: Distant boat wakes barely visible; wake RT 3000 m.
entries.defect: src/render/wakes.ts:12-14: the WakeMap is a single 1024x1024 UnsignedByteType target spanning 3200 m (3.1 m per texel, 8-bit foam), so wakes are blurry near the hull, identical in shape and quantised.
entries.fix: Use two wake cascades (near 800 m at 1024, far 3200 m) in HalfFloatType with foam break-up noise, and write static footprints for moored hulls.

entries.evidence: Low-poly puffs; all tiles drawn.
entries.defect: src/world/vegetation.ts: canopies are icosahedron puffs (high triangle count), every tile is drawn (bounding-sphere bug at line 328), updateLod() thins instance count in hard steps at 2000/3500/5000 m (t.mesh.count) so trees pop in and out along the flight path, and frondTexture() uses Math.random (line 16) so the palm texture differs between runs.
entries.fix: Add billboard/impostor LOD beyond ~1.5 km with a dithered cross-fade instead of count steps, use a local bounding sphere so tiles cull, cast shadows only from tiles within 1.5 km using a low-poly proxy, and seed frondTexture() through the Rng class.

entries.evidence: Reads as a ribbon; polygonOffset defeated by log depth.
entries.defect: src/world/roads.ts:215 relies on polygonOffset(-2,-2) while game.ts creates the renderer with logarithmicDepthBuffer:true; writing gl_FragDepth disables fixed-function polygon offset, so roads placed only 0.12 m above heightAt() z-fight / sink where the coarser terrain rings deviate more than 0.12 m; bridge hangers/railings are thin single-pixel geometry with frustumCulled=false.
entries.fix: Apply the offset in the shader (gl_FragDepth -= bias scaled by slope) or drop the logarithmic depth buffer (reversed-Z / tighter near plane), lift roads by the terrain ring error, and give hangers a minimum screen width (or fade them by distance).

entries.evidence: Cloud puffs are small grainy blobs with speckled edges.
entries.defect: src/world/sky.ts: the volumetric raymarch uses uCloudSteps=24 (high) at skyScale 0.6 (0.6x resolution) with a per-pixel jitter hash12(gl_FragCoord.xy) that is static in time and never filtered, so under-sampled density shows as fixed-pattern grain and the 0.6x buffer is bilinearly upsampled; the cloud layer is faded with smoothstep(0.012,0.06,dir.y), producing a straight seam above the horizon.
entries.fix: Animate the jitter with a blue-noise texture indexed by frame and accumulate temporally (reprojection), or raise steps adaptively with transmittance early-out; upsample with a depth/transmittance-aware bilateral filter; replace the linear horizon fade by a curvature/distance fade so the seam follows the haze.

entries.evidence: Skyline shows a mild blue shift but the horizon is a crisp line; land lacks haze layering.
entries.defect: src/world/water.ts builds a 70 km PlaneGeometry(48x48) that ends before the sky dome (camera.far*0.9 = 54 km) so at altitude the plane's far edge shows as a hard line against the dome; applyAerial in src/render/post.ts reconstructs from depth and leaves distant land/water with too little haze contrast.
entries.fix: Use a camera-following radial/projected-grid water mesh that reaches the dome (or clip the dome to the water horizon), and increase haze density with altitude-dependent optical depth so land and water converge to the horizon colour.

entries.evidence: Exterior slightly hot, interior panel readable; no eye adaptation.

entries.fix: Add view-dependent exposure or brighter interior fill.

entries.evidence: Interior boxes cast shadows with the CSM (castShadow=true) causing minor acne on the glareshield; exterior shadows unresolvable.
entries.defect: 3 cascades x 2048 over maxFar 3500-3600 m (probe: texel 0.55 / 1.17 / 3.28 m, normalBias 1.5 texel, bias -0.0002) - the far cascade resolves buildings as 3 m blocks; game.ts:257 re-splits the cascades whenever altitude*9 crosses a 200 m band, city/vegetation updateLod() toggles castShadow per tile at a hard distance, and terrain never casts shadows (terrain.ts castShadow=false).
entries.fix: Use 4 cascades with a smoothed (lerped) maxFar and CSM fade:true, PCF with a fixed world-space filter radius, enable terrain shadow casting for the near ring, and fade caster tiles over a 300 m band instead of toggling.

entries.evidence: No sun highlight or environment reflection in any pane.
entries.defect: src/plane/model.ts:59-73: the glass is one DoubleSide MeshPhysicalMaterial mesh with depthWrite=false, opacity driven by an ad-hoc (1-NdotV)^3 alpha ramp (0.22 -> 0.85) instead of a reflectance Fresnel, so panes darken/turn opaque at grazing angles rather than becoming mirror-like; overlapping panes inside a single mesh are composited in triangle order (mis-sorting), the loft faces are flat-shaded so the ramp is faceted, and the PMREM environment is a sky-only dome (no sun disc), so there is no sun highlight in the glass.
entries.fix: Keep alpha constant (~0.15) and let specular Fresnel (specularIntensity/ior, clearcoat) carry the view dependence; render inner and outer glass as two FrontSide meshes with renderOrder outer>inner; smooth the glass normals (computeVertexNormals on the indexed loft before splitGlass); add the sun disc/skyRadiance to the envScene so reflections carry a highlight.

entries.evidence: Neutral; slightly cyan sky.

entries.fix: Replace the fixed lift/gain in COMPOSITE_FRAG with a per-time-of-day/weather LUT (or ACES/AgX + exposure uniform) and reduce the teal push on mid-tones.

entries.condition: renderer.info counters and 8-frame synchronous profile vs a 60 FPS desktop budget (<=400 calls, <=1.5 M tris). Frames come from headless Chrome on SwiftShader (software rasterizer), so absolute frame times (3-5 s per 1080p frame) are not representative of a desktop GPU; relative cost, counters and spread are evaluated instead.
entries.evidence: renderer.info: 1293 draw calls (3.2x the 400-call budget), 6.48 M triangles (4.3x the 1.5 M budget), 585 geometries, 36 textures, 40 programs, JS heap 143 MB; bench profile of 8 synchronous frames: avg 4894 ms, min 4821, max 4985 (spread 3.4% of avg). Probe (toggling scene groups on the same build, 960x540, counters are resolution independent): shadow pass = 636 calls / 2.94 M tris; vegetation = 252 calls / 4.27 M tris (66% of all triangles); city = 325 calls / 0.61 M; props = 77 calls / 0.76 M; traffic = 196 calls / 0.19 M; aircraft = 347 calls for only 22 k tris; camera pointed at the zenith still draws 992 calls / 6.42 M tris (frustum culling is effectively off). console.txt is 0 bytes for all 13 views (no shader-compile, texture, WebGL or deprecation messages during capture) and the probe pages logged nothing either.
entries.defect: Every view is 2.7-3.8x over the draw-call budget and 2.4-5.9x over the triangle budget: (a) frustum culling is defeated - src/world/vegetation.ts:328 and src/world/city.ts:170 store a WORLD-space sphere in geometry.boundingSphere, which InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere() then transforms by every instance matrix (centre x scale ~10, radius km) so no tile is ever culled, while props.ts:69/75, traffic.ts:306 (all cars), game.ts:175 (lamps), bridges.ts:217-232, roads.ts:210 set frustumCulled=false; (b) the 3-cascade CSM re-draws every caster up to 3 more times (shadow pass = 30-57% of triangles); (c) icosahedron-puff canopies make vegetation 43-72% of all triangles; (d) the aircraft is ~85 separate meshes (232-444 draw calls for ~22 k triangles). Frame-time spread in this view is 3.4% of the mean (no streaming stutter observed). Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
entries.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).

entries.evidence: Towers have clear hierarchy; facades resolve as flat colour with aliased window rows; blocky shadows; suburbs are a field of 1-2 px house specks whose colour is randomised per pixel by the facade.ts roof branch flip (verified in cloudy).
entries.defect: src/world/facade.ts: window/tile patterns are step() functions of world position with only a fwidth-based 'lod' blend applied to colour; the emissive term (lines 118/129/143/157/180) is not attenuated by lod, and MSAA does not filter shader aliasing, so sub-pixel windows and 0.35 m tile rows alias into speckle at distance. src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding.
entries.fix: Multiply emis by (1.0 - lod) and blend to the average lit fraction, pre-filter the patterns analytically (box-filtered step) or bake facades to a mip-mapped atlas; add TAA or increase MSAA for thin geometry. Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback.

entries.condition: Hotel towers along the beach and houses behind them.
entries.evidence: Towers are clean boxes with aliased window rows; distant hotels are flat specks; houses behind the strip are not resolvable here, but the facade.ts roof branch flip (verified in cloudy) applies to every house roof.
entries.defect: src/world/facade.ts: window/tile patterns are step() functions of world position with only a fwidth-based 'lod' blend applied to colour; the emissive term (lines 118/129/143/157/180) is not attenuated by lod, and MSAA does not filter shader aliasing, so sub-pixel windows and 0.35 m tile rows alias into speckle at distance. src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding.
entries.fix: Multiply emis by (1.0 - lod) and blend to the average lit fraction, pre-filter the patterns analytically (box-filtered step) or bake facades to a mip-mapped atlas; add TAA or increase MSAA for thin geometry. Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback.

entries.evidence: Hidden by the box.
entries.defect: src/plane/model.ts:59-73: the glass is one DoubleSide MeshPhysicalMaterial mesh with depthWrite=false, opacity driven by an ad-hoc (1-NdotV)^3 alpha ramp (0.22 -> 0.85) instead of a reflectance Fresnel, so panes darken/turn opaque at grazing angles rather than becoming mirror-like; overlapping panes inside a single mesh are composited in triangle order (mis-sorting), the loft faces are flat-shaded so the ramp is faceted, and the PMREM environment is a sky-only dome (no sun disc), so there is no sun highlight in the glass.

entries.evidence: Clean towers; facades alias.

entries.condition: renderer.info counters and 8-frame synchronous profile vs a 60 FPS desktop budget (<=400 calls, <=1.5 M tris). Frames come from headless Chrome on SwiftShader (software rasterizer), so absolute frame times (3-5 s per 1080p frame) are not representative of a desktop GPU; relative cost, counters and spread are evaluated instead.
entries.evidence: renderer.info: 1357 draw calls (3.4x the 400-call budget), 8.49 M triangles (5.7x the 1.5 M budget), 534 geometries, 39 textures, 40 programs, JS heap 142 MB; bench profile of 8 synchronous frames: avg 3831 ms, min 3737, max 4043 (spread 8.0% of avg). Probe (toggling scene groups on the same build, 960x540, counters are resolution independent): shadow pass = 644 calls / 4.88 M tris; vegetation = 294 calls / 6.11 M tris (72% of all triangles); city = 335 calls / 0.77 M; props = 77 calls / 0.76 M; traffic = 217 calls / 0.19 M; aircraft = 338 calls for only 22 k tris; camera pointed at the zenith still draws 960 calls / 8.46 M tris (frustum culling is effectively off). console.txt is 0 bytes for all 13 views (no shader-compile, texture, WebGL or deprecation messages during capture) and the probe pages logged nothing either.
entries.defect: Every view is 2.7-3.8x over the draw-call budget and 2.4-5.9x over the triangle budget: (a) frustum culling is defeated - src/world/vegetation.ts:328 and src/world/city.ts:170 store a WORLD-space sphere in geometry.boundingSphere, which InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere() then transforms by every instance matrix (centre x scale ~10, radius km) so no tile is ever culled, while props.ts:69/75, traffic.ts:306 (all cars), game.ts:175 (lamps), bridges.ts:217-232, roads.ts:210 set frustumCulled=false; (b) the 3-cascade CSM re-draws every caster up to 3 more times (shadow pass = 30-57% of triangles); (c) icosahedron-puff canopies make vegetation 43-72% of all triangles; (d) the aircraft is ~85 separate meshes (232-444 draw calls for ~22 k triangles). Frame-time spread in this view is 8.0% of the mean (no streaming stutter observed). Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
entries.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).

entries.evidence: Hidden by box; no sun highlight.
entries.defect: src/plane/model.ts:59-73: the glass is one DoubleSide MeshPhysicalMaterial mesh with depthWrite=false, opacity driven by an ad-hoc (1-NdotV)^3 alpha ramp (0.22 -> 0.85) instead of a reflectance Fresnel, so panes darken/turn opaque at grazing angles rather than becoming mirror-like; overlapping panes inside a single mesh are composited in triangle order (mis-sorting), the loft faces are flat-shaded so the ramp is faceted, and the PMREM environment is a sky-only dome (no sun disc), so there is no sun highlight in the glass.

entries.evidence: Far mainland shows periodic rows of dark dots (houses/trees) - moire; the facade.ts roof branch flip (verified in cloudy) randomises the colour of the few-pixel house specks.
entries.defect: src/world/facade.ts: window/tile patterns are step() functions of world position with only a fwidth-based 'lod' blend applied to colour; the emissive term (lines 118/129/143/157/180) is not attenuated by lod, and MSAA does not filter shader aliasing, so sub-pixel windows and 0.35 m tile rows alias into speckle at distance. src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding.
entries.fix: Multiply emis by (1.0 - lod) and blend to the average lit fraction, pre-filter the patterns analytically (box-filtered step) or bake facades to a mip-mapped atlas; add TAA or increase MSAA for thin geometry. Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback.

Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. entries.fix: Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback.

entries.defect: src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding. src/world/sky.ts: the volumetric raymarch uses uCloudSteps=24 (high) at skyScale 0.6 (0.6x resolution) with a per-pixel jitter hash12(gl_FragCoord.xy) that is static in time and never filtered, so under-sampled density shows as fixed-pattern grain and the 0.6x buffer is bilinearly upsampled; the cloud layer is faded with smoothstep(0.012,0.06,dir.y), producing a straight seam above the horizon.

entries.defect: Every view is 2.7-3.8x over the draw-call budget and 2.4-5.9x over the triangle budget: (a) frustum culling is defeated - src/world/vegetation.ts:328 and src/world/city.ts:170 store a WORLD-space sphere in geometry.boundingSphere, which InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere() then transforms by every instance matrix (centre x scale ~10, radius km) so no tile is ever culled, while props.ts:69/75, traffic.ts:306 (all cars), game.ts:175 (lamps), bridges.ts:217-232, roads.ts:210 set frustumCulled=false; (b) the 3-cascade CSM re-draws every caster up to 3 more times (shadow pass = 30-57% of triangles); (c) icosahedron-puff canopies make vegetation 43-72% of all triangles; (d) the aircraft is ~85 separate meshes (232-444 draw calls for ~22 k triangles). Frame-time spread in this view is 5.7% of the mean (no streaming stutter observed). Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
entries.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).
